title: Are Hogs Nocturnal? When the Sounder Comes to Your Trap
support_keywords: what time do hogs come out
reader_sentence: Hogs mostly come to your trap after dark, and later the more they've been pressured, so watch it live for a few nights to learn when the whole sounder shows up, then be ready to close it at that hour instead of checking it in the morning.

evidence.signal: are hogs nocturnal 70/mo, are wild hogs nocturnal 70, wild hog behavior 70, when are feral hogs most active 50, when are hogs most active 40, what time do hogs come out 40

key_points: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension says feral hogs are routinely nocturnal during summer heat.
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension says that in winter, hogs may become more active during the daytime as they search for food.
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension says hunting pressure can leave a sounder that is rarely seen in daylight, in any season.
The whole sounder does not always arrive together, so counting hogs over several nights tells you how many there are before you close.
The HogEye Mini Camera streams live video to the HogEye app, day or night, with digital pan, tilt, and zoom.
The camera sends a motion alert to your phone when hogs come into the trap.
Recordings stay on the camera for 14 days, so you can look back at what time the hogs came in each night.
You watch the hogs inside and outside the trap in the app, and when the whole sounder is inside you send the close command from your phone and the gate closes.
Closing on part of a sounder teaches the hogs that got away to avoid the trap.
h2_outline: Count them for a few nights
